The note: "[2026-05-22] standup/dune/2026-05-22: Tomasz picked up the Dune on-call shift from Farah today."

This is a durable fact: As of 2026-05-22, Tomasz holds the Dune team on-call shift, taking over from Farah.

Existing facts: memory_id "1001207": As of 2026-04-14, Farah holds the Dune team pager, taking over from Tomasz. This is about the pager, not on-call shift. The note says Tomasz picked up the Dune on-call shift from Farah. Is the on-call shift the same as the pager? Looking at history: memory 1000923 "Tomasz holds the Dune team pager this cycle, taking over from Farah" and 1000678 "Tomasz holds the Dune team on-call shift, taking over from Farah" — these seem to be treated as separate facts (pager vs on-call shift). Actually they're separate memories. Hmm, but they might be considered the same thing. The existing memory store keeps them separate. The note says "on-call shift", so it parallels 1000678 style.

Should we correct 1001207 (Farah holds the Dune team pager)? The note says Tomasz picked up the on-call shift from Farah. If pager and on-call shift are the same thing, then this would correct 1001207. But the memory store distinguishes them. Given the pattern, I think the safest is to add a new fact: "As of 2026-05-22, Tomasz holds the Dune team on-call shift, taking over from Farah." with entities Tomasz, Farah, Dune team.

Should we also correct 1001207? The note implies Farah no longer holds the pager/on-call. Hmm. The instruction: "When the note changes something an existing fact states, do not add a contradicting fact. Add a correction..." The existing fact 1001207 says "As of 2026-04-14, Farah holds the Dune team pager, taking over from Tomasz." The note changes the current holder. If pager == on-call shift, then the new fact contradicts. But the store has both pager facts and on-call shift facts coexisting (1000923 pager, 1000678 on-call shift, both about the same period roughly — 1000923 as of 2025-12-10, 1000678 as of 2025-09-04; different dates though). Actually 1000786: 2025-10-15 Farah holds pager taking over from Tomasz; 1000678: 2025-09-04 Tomasz holds on-call shift taking over from Farah. These are different cycles, so no contradiction.

Given the store treats "pager" and "on-call shift" as distinct facts, and the note says "on-call shift", I'll add a new fact about the on-call shift. Should I also correct the pager fact? The note doesn't mention the pager. I'll be conservative: add the new fact only. But arguably the on-call shift and pager are the same duty; the note says Tomasz picked it up from Farah, which supersedes 1001207. Hmm.

The guidance: "When the note changes something an existing fact states, do not add a contradicting fact." The new fact "As of 2026-05-22, Tomasz holds the Dune team on-call shift, taking over from Farah" doesn't directly contradict "As of 2026-04-14, Farah holds the Dune team pager" because they're dated snapshots. The existing facts are all phrased as "As of DATE, X holds..." — they're point-in-time facts, not current-state facts. So adding a new dated fact is consistent with the store's pattern.

So: add_facts with one entry:
- content: "As of 2026-05-22, Tomasz holds the Dune team on-call shift, taking over from Farah."
- entities: ["Tomasz", "Farah", "Dune team"]
- kind: "fact"
- confidence: 1
- evidence: "Tomasz picked up the Dune on-call shift from Farah today."

Relations? The note establishes Tomasz takes over on-call from Farah — is that a relation? Relations like "leads, maintains, owns, depends_on, member_of". On-call shift isn't really a relation between entities. Previous pattern probably didn't add relations for pager handovers. I'll skip relations.

Aliases: "Dune on-call shift" — refers to Dune team's on-call shift; not an entity alias needed. No.

Output single JSON object.
